reasoning_traces.think:
These sovereign primitives arise from the fundamental challenge of isolating causal effects in non-randomized sports interventions. Difference-in-differences exploits parallel trends between treated and control groups, assuming that without the rule change, outcomes would have evolved similarly. Synthetic control analysis constructs a weighted composite of untreated units to serve as a counterfactual, while interrupted time series examines abrupt changes in level or slope at the intervention point. Failure modes include autocorrelation, pre-existing trend differences, and anticipation effects, which can bias estimates. These methods are duals of each other under certain linear constraints, forming a unified framework for quasi-experimental inference.
